messages:
Maya (PM): Kicking off a quick thread to align on the long-horizon routing/tenant isolation roadmap. I sketched three scenarios (steady, bursty, and fragmented onramp) in the doc: https://redwood.internal/roadmaps/routing-longview-v1 — want input on launch criteria and the prioritization rubric.

Alex (Eng): skimmed the doc. scenarios make sense. main question: how strict do we want isolation for steady vs fragmented? steady customers expect stable latency SLAs; fragmented are more tolerant but higher churn.

Chen (Infra): agree. steady ~= reserved capacity / Dedicated guarantees. that implies node fencing + affinity lanes. cost delta is significant. need a gate for minimum commit size to justify isolation lanes.

Iris (SRE): ops perspective: runbooks must define deterministic failover. for steady customers require cross-region redundancy (N+1) and evacuation playbook. for fragmented/onramp fallback to best-effort hosted models is acceptable.

Sam (Product Ops): Sales update: large fintech (P1) needs regional isolation + KMS before onboarding. small customers want a low-cost dev tier with weaker SLA. prioritize P1 but offer a migration path for midsize.

Maya (PM): Draft launch criteria: Stability: 99.9% p95 latency under committed load; Resilience: cross-region failover tested in staging; Security: KMS + audit logs for Private/Dedicated; Economics: cost model validated with 2 anchor customers. Which are blockers vs nice-to-have?

Alex (Eng): Blockers: hit latency target and ensure KV cache correctness under eviction. Nice-to-have: billing SKU UX polish.

Chen (Infra): Blockers: KMS handshake and network onboarding automation. Also propose capacity commit thresholds, e.g., >=4 reserved GPUs or sustained 200k tokens/min to qualify for an isolated lane.

Iris (SRE): Add ops gate: runbook automation and test drills are blockers for steady lanes. Canary + automatic rollback required pre-GA.

Sam (Product Ops): Prioritization rubric suggestion: Customer risk (revenue/strategic) 40%; Complexity (eng+infra effort) 30%; Time-to-value (weeks to onboard) 20%; Compliance/regulatory need 10%. This pushes P1 high.

Alex (Eng): ok with weights. add "operational cost delta" under complexity — plateau lanes may be 2-3x unit cost.

Maya (PM): Revised phase proposal: phase 1 = Private with KMS + single-region tenant shielding; phase 2 = cross-region replication + automated evacuation; phase 3 = self-serve Reserved Lanes in console. Objections?

Chen (Infra): timeline: phase 1 ~8–10w (KMS + network onboarding + tenant fencing), phase 2 ~10–12w (replication + evacuation tooling), phase 3 ~6–8w (console + billing). rough estimates.

Iris (SRE): ops burden grows across phases. include an Ops Readiness gate per phase: runbook, SLO alerting, oncall rehearsal.

Sam (Product Ops): Sales requests an "onramp path" doc for P1 outlining commitments/timeline + fallback plan. I'll draft once phase 1 gates are locked.

Maya (PM): Action items:
- Maya: update the roadmap doc with blockers/gates and prioritization rubric (due EOD Friday)
- Alex: prototype eviction-safe KV cache changes and perf test plan (P0) due in 2 weeks
- Chen: draft capacity commit thresholds and automation plan (due next Wed)
- Iris: produce Ops readiness checklist per phase (due next Mon)
- Sam: prepare customer onramp stub for P1 (due next Wed)

deploy-bot: Scheduled: /deploy canary routing-lane v0.9 to staging at 2024-05-03T04:00:00Z

Alex (Eng): noted the deploy. we'll include canary test matrix in perf plan.

Maya (PM): please comment inline on the doc; will consolidate and present at roadmap sync on Tue if no objections. :thumbsup:

Chen (Infra): please include estimated incremental infra $/q for steady lanes so finance can price.

Sam (Product Ops): +1 to finance ask and loop in legal for KMS controls.

Iris (SRE): will schedule a tabletop evacuation drill after phase 2 prototype is up.

Maya (PM): sending calendar invites after doc update. End of thread.
